thread:
natalie: Heads-up — I pushed a draft checklist for the audit-event schema regression tests and a short customer preview note. Need quick reviews before EOD.
alex: link?
mira: thanks. sharing the PR url in #eng-releases too?
natalie: https://git.internal/r/redwood/audit-schema/pull/814 — the checklist is in the PR description.
samir: skimmed the PR. main question: did we include KMS key id redaction rules for private deployments? last customer asked about KMS ARNs in logs.
natalie: yes — we added a redaction policy and sample mapping. excerpt in the PR: `event.secrets_redacted: true` and we also normalize kms_key_id -> `kms_key_fingerprint` in the audit schema.
frank: can you paste the example event here? makes reviews faster.
natalie: sure, pasted below:
```json
{
  "event_type": "model.load",
  "actor": "service_account:inference-router",
  "resource": "model:vicuna-13b:rev3",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-19T18:42:31Z",
  "metadata": {
    "request_id": "req_abc123",
    "kms_key_fingerprint": "sha256:3f5...c9a"
  },
  "secrets_redacted": true
}
```
mira: nice. for customer-facing validation we should include a mapping table that lists old field -> new field and a compatibility note. some customers are still ingesting `kms_key_id`.
jordan: also add a sample Splunk/Kinesis ingestion rule so they can map easily, + a short regex to accept both forms while they transition.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist: automated schema tests: 42 passed, 1 flaky (audit-event.timing-metrics).
samir: that flaky test is the prefix-caching latency metric — it's jittery in nightly envs. I can take a look.
frank: what's the message we'll send to customers? I can help draft the notice. keep it short and include migration snippet.
natalie: draft customer preview (very short):
"We are updating the audit event schema to improve KMS field privacy and normalize key identifiers. Migration window: 30 days. New field: `kms_key_fingerprint`. We will continue to emit `kms_key_id` for 30 days with compatibility metadata. See migration examples and quick mapping in the linked PR."
alex: add an opt-out note for Private customers who need air-gapped migrations.
mira: and a line about how this helps security/compliance reviews (no raw ARNs in logs).
jordan: sample migration snippet for Splunk: `eval kms_key_fingerprint=coalesce(kms_key_fingerprint, sha256(kms_key_id))` — maybe too hand-wavy.
samir: probably fine. Ops teams will implement their own fingerprinting. we should say "do not rely on unhashed ARNs in logs".
frank: can we add a short runbook for incident response? what to do if someone spots `kms_key_id` in logs after rollout.
natalie: runbook bullet: 1) tag source events with `migration_unmapped:true`, 2) rotate the KMS key if ARNs leak, notify security, 3) run extraction job to find all exposures and notify affected customers.
ops-bot: note: scheduled rollout job created for 2026-03-22 01:00 UTC.
mira: one more ask — include a small regression checklist for SDK event publishers (python/node). we had a regression last time where `request_id` moved from metadata -> top-level.
frank: yes, add unit test examples, sample payload asserts: `assert 'kms_key_fingerprint' in event['metadata']` and `assert 'kms_key_id' not in persisted_event['metadata']` (after redaction).
jordan: I'll add the Splunk snippet and a Kinesis JSON schema example.
samir: for release notes: short line plus link to migration guide. Keep legal/compliance in loop. cc @mira.
mira: pinged legal in #people-ops-legal.
natalie: thanks folks. plan: patch PR with customer note and runbook updates by 5pm PT, merge, and then prep a staging rollout tomorrow.
frank: :thumbsup:
samir: I'll triage the flaky test today.
natalie: sending a follow-up thread to eng-release after merge with exact rollout job ids.
ops-bot: deploy: PR #814 merged to staging by natalie at 2026-03-19T19:05:12Z.
